tasks.short: Count participation per group and age, talk with leaders about the congregation's changing emphasis, analyze needs for religious education, write a needs note and send it to the council.

steps.what: Group leaders tick attendance in the member register at each session; a paper list today
Religious education director counts participation per group and age from paper lists
Religious education director talks with leaders and reads council minutes about changes in congregational emphasis
Religious education director analyzes member participation to determine needs for religious education
Religious education director writes a short needs note for the council
Religious education director checks the final needs note: figures per group against the view, the analysis and the council it goes to
Religious education director sends the checked needs note to the council

tasks.design: A participation view over the member register ({OTHER}) shows group attendance, age cohorts, new members and moves, so figures are not counted from paper lists. The needs note is a template that pulls in those figures; the director writes the analysis and checks the note before it goes to the council. Talking with leaders and judging needs stay with the director; figures are shown per group, never per named member outside the congregation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Participation was counted by hand from paper lists and member spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Church member registers hold group membership and stay current through the municipal register link.
tasks.still_hard: Registers miss people who take part but never register.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing that young parents want something other than what the figures suggest.

ambition.what: Review education needs every quarter instead of once a year.

tasks.altitude: The director interprets figures instead of counting them.

reach.learn: Whether current figures change council choices.

evidence.claim: LRP, the Protestant member register, receives moves and deaths from the municipal register through SILA.
The Roermond diocese reports gaps in the shared member register, mainly young Catholics, because some parishes do not register new members.
Church membership reveals religious belief, a special category; it may not be disclosed outside the body without consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from attendance and member lists to the note sent; designing programmes is outside.

Input contract for s1: attendance ticked per session by group leaders in the member register (s6), with about the effort of the paper list; member data from the member administrator; fallback is paper lists.
Talking with leaders and judging needs do not change.
Figures are shown per group and age band.
Coverage: about 70% of group leaders tick attendance in the register; the director still counts the paper lists of the rest, so s1 keeps 45%.
s4 keeps 75 because the director writes the analysis; the template only pulls in the figures. s5 keeps 20 for the send.
research_questions: Do unregistered participants distort the figures?

already_counted.description: Religious education director reads the participation view.

incremental.description: Religious education director reminds leaders to tick attendance.

approvals.approved_version: The needs note with its figures and analysis exactly as checked by the director in s4b, sent once to the church council; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only about 30% of leaders tick attendance in the register, so s1 keeps 76 (11.0); high: 70% tick as in A4 (19.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Get revenue and cost figures from the treasurer, put costs per programme together, compare costs per participant, determine budget priorities and propose the education budget to the council.

steps.what: Religious education director asks the treasurer for revenue and cost figures
Religious education director puts revenue and program cost data per programme in a spreadsheet
Religious education director compares costs per participant across programmes
Religious education director determines budget priorities for the education programmes
Religious education director proposes the education budget in the council meeting

tasks.design: Programme costs are booked to cost centres in the church's accounting package ({ERP}), and a read-only view gives the director revenue and costs per programme, so nothing is requested or copied by hand. The same view divides costs by participants from the member register. Setting priorities and proposing the budget stay with the director.
tasks.previous_blocker: Figures came from the treasurer by e-mail and were rebuilt in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Church administration packages link member, contribution and financial records.
tasks.still_hard: Costs shared between programmes need an agreed split.
tasks.human_edge: Defending a small programme that matters more than its cost per head suggests.
tasks.altitude: The director sets priorities from ready figures instead of building them.

reach.learn: Whether cost centres per programme cut questions.

evidence.claim: DocBase keeps member, church-contribution, cemetery and financial administration in one set for Catholic parishes.
Churches with ANBI status publish financial data online.

assumptions: Boundary: from accounting records to the proposed budget; the council's decision is outside.

Input contract for s3: bookings per cost centre by the treasurer; participants per programme from the attendance group leaders tick in the member register, a capture counted in the needs task; fallback is e-mail and spreadsheets.
Setting priorities and proposing do not change.
The treasurer sets up cost centres once; that time is outside the director's savings.
unknowns: Programmes with their own cost centre.
research_questions: Do budget discussions start from the same figures?

already_counted.description: Religious education director reviews the cost view.

incremental.description: Religious education director checks bookings that land on the wrong programme.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half of the costs are booked without programme codes, so the director still asks and sorts them, and s1 keeps 60 and s2 keeps 50 (27.5); high: every programme on its own cost centre (44.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Find and choose workshops and conferences, register and arrange travel, attend them for programme ideas and resources, and write up ideas for colleagues.

steps.what: Religious education director finds and chooses workshops, seminars and conferences
Religious education director checks the registration and travel before booking: event, dates, costs within the training budget
Religious education director registers and arranges travel
Religious education director attends workshops, seminars or conferences to obtain program ideas
Religious education director writes up programme ideas and resources for colleagues

tasks.design: The denomination's events calendar lists workshops and conferences by theme, and registration goes through the organisers' online forms. Ideas and resources go into a shared idea page in the document space ({DOCS}) with a short template, so colleagues find them later. Attending stays with the director.
tasks.previous_blocker: Events were found through newsletters and notes kept in personal files.
tasks.enabler_now: Denominations publish event calendars; shared document spaces hold idea pages.
tasks.still_hard: The best ideas come from conversations in the corridor.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting the idea that will work in this congregation.

reach.learn: Whether shared idea pages get used.

evidence.claim: Shared document spaces can hold idea pages with a fixed template.

assumptions: Boundary: from learning needs to idea notes; putting ideas into practice is outside.
Input contract: event calendars from the denomination; fallback is newsletters.
Attending and the check before booking do not change. s4 keeps 90 because the director writes up the ideas; the template only gives the layout.
Organisers' time is outside the director's savings.
research_questions: Do colleagues use the idea pages?

incremental.description: Religious education director tags idea pages by theme.

approvals.approved_version: The registration and travel bookings with event, dates and costs exactly as checked by the director in s1b within the training budget, booked once with the organiser and travel provider; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the denomination's calendar lists few relevant events, so the director still searches and s1 keeps 90 (6.1); high: calendar as designed (9.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Pick new members and families to visit, phone to arrange visits, arrange pastoral visits by volunteers, visit members' homes about religious education, and note visits and follow-up.

steps.what: Religious education director picks new members and families with children to visit
Religious education director phones members to arrange a home visit
Religious education director assigns pastoral visits to volunteer visitors in the register's pastoral module; by e-mail today
Religious education director checks the assignments: family, visitor, date and what the visitor may know
Religious education director releases the checked assignments; the module notifies the visitors
Religious education director visits congregational members' homes to provide information on religious education programs
Religious education director notes the visit and agreed follow-up

tasks.design: The member register ({OTHER}) lists new members and families with children of programme age, kept current through the municipal register link, so the visit list is not built by hand. Volunteer visits are assigned in the register's pastoral module, which notifies visitors, after the director checks and releases them, and visit notes are written there as today, with access limited to the pastoral team; this first record keeps its time. Arranging and making visits stay with the director.
tasks.previous_blocker: Visit lists were built from spreadsheets and volunteer visits arranged by e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Church member registers include pastoral modules with restricted access.
tasks.still_hard: Families who are hard to reach by phone stay hard to reach.
tasks.human_edge: Sensing at the kitchen table what a family is really asking for.

reach.learn: Whether assigned visits get made sooner.

evidence.claim: LRP, the Protestant member register, receives moves and deaths from the municipal register through SILA.
Church membership reveals religious belief; a religious body may process it for members but not disclose it outside without consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the member list to visit notes; enrolling children in programmes is outside.
Input contract: member data from the register kept by the member administrator; fallback is spreadsheets.
Phoning, visiting, checking assignments and noting visits do not change.
Volunteer visitors' time is outside the director's savings.

incremental.description: Religious education director keeps visitor assignments current.

approvals.approved_version: The visit assignments with family, visitor and date exactly as checked by the director in s3b, notified once to those volunteer visitors through the pastoral module; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small congregation where the director knows every family and arranges visits by phone, so s1 and s3 keep 80 (5.1); high: register and module as designed (12.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The religious education director keeps judging needs, setting priorities and visiting families; counting from paper lists, rebuilding budgets and arranging visits by e-mail shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A director who reviews needs every quarter and spends saved time on visits.
